title: England dominate Pakistan, close in on Test series sweep

article.title: England dominate Pakistan, close in on Test series sweep
article.summary: Ruthless England tamed Pakistan’s inexperienced attack in the third Test at Edgbaston on Thursday to move to the brink of a series whitewash against their hapless opponents. Joe Root’s men, already 2-0 up in the three-match contest, were dismissed for 453 on the second day of the match to take a first-innings lead of 320, threatening to wrap up victory in double-quick time. England rattled along on a sunny morning in Birmingham, with Dan Lawrence reaching his half-century off just 47 balls, hitting eight fours. But their progress was checked when Harry Brook needlessly ran himself out for 75 when in sight of an 11th Test century. Brook tossed his bat into the air in frustration as his partnership with Lawrence was ended at 86, leaving England 229-5. The scoring slowed briefly after Jamie Smith arrived at the crease but he soon showed his attacking intent, launching the ball straight back over the head of spinner Saim Ayub for six. Lawrence (65) chopped a ball from Mohammad Imran onto his stumps shortly before lunch to give the all-rounder his first Test wicket.
